event: US housing starts & building permits (October)
why: Home building drives rebar, copper wire and aluminum demand.

event: FOMC minutes (Oct 27-28 meeting)
why: Tone on a December hike moves the dollar, which has been pushing copper, gold and PGMs lower.

event: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey (November)
why: Early read on factory activity, a driver of industrial scrap generation and metal demand.

event: US weekly initial jobless claims
why: Labor data feeds Fed hike expectations and the dollar.
source: Letters to a Young Investor (weekly calendar)

event: China loan prime rate (November; date listed as estimated)
why: A cut would signal more support for China's property sector and metals demand.

event: University of Michigan consumer sentiment (final November)
why: Consumer mood and inflation expectations shape Fed policy and big-ticket spending like cars.
source: Letters to a Young Investor (weekly calendar)

event: S&P Global flash US manufacturing & services PMIs (November)
why: First look at November factory activity and steel/metal demand.

event: Nucor weekly hot-rolled coil spot price (CSP) and AISI weekly raw steel output
why: Shows whether the 18-week HRC rally and high mill run rates that support scrap demand are continuing.

event: Conference Board consumer confidence (November)
why: Gauges household demand for autos and housing.

event: Q3 GDP (second estimate) and October personal income/PCE inflation
why: PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge and will shape December hike odds and the dollar.

event: Durable goods orders (October)
why: Tracks orders for metal-heavy equipment and vehicles.

event: New home sales (October) and preliminary US steel imports (October)
why: Housing demand drives construction metals; steel import volumes show pressure on domestic mill prices.

event: Federal Reserve Beige Book
why: Regional notes on manufacturing, construction and steel demand ahead of the Dec 8-9 FOMC.

event: Thanksgiving: US stock and bond markets closed; CME publishes no settlements for COMEX/NYMEX
why: No US metals price discovery; expect thin trading around the holiday.

event: Advance economic indicators (October trade in goods, inventories); shortened US trading day
why: Goods trade data shows import and export flows, including metals; light holiday volume can exaggerate moves.

event: Nucor weekly CSP and AISI weekly raw steel output
why: Last read on mill pricing and output before December scrap trading settles.

event: ISM manufacturing PMI (November), construction spending (October), JOLTS (October)
why: Factory and construction activity drive scrap generation and metals demand.

event: ISM services PMI (November) and factory orders (October)
why: Broad demand check ahead of the Fed meeting.

event: US jobs report (November)
why: Last major data before the Dec 8-9 FOMC; a strong report would lift the dollar and weigh on metals.

event: FOMC rate decision (Dec 8-9 meeting, with projections)
why: Markets expect a hike, so a hawkish outcome would pressure copper, gold and PGMs.
